findings.title: Missing integration rows bypass installer verification
findings.body: When no Integration row exists for the supplied installation_id, this branch advances the pipeline without comparing the authenticated GitHub user to the installer. The pipeline then retrieves the installation using app credentials in build_integration, which does not verify the user either. Thus a user authenticated to any GitHub account can claim an installation whose webhook has not yet created its Integration row (for example, during webhook delivery delays). Fail closed or verify the user's authority over the installation before advancing this branch.

findings.title: Handle integrations without sender metadata
findings.body: The installer check unconditionally indexes integration.metadata["sender"]["login"], but sender is optional in build_integration, and the basic installation flow in this PR explicitly produces metadata without it. If such an Integration remains after its OrganizationIntegration is removed, attempting to reconnect it now raises KeyError and returns a server error instead of completing or displaying the authenticity error. Handle missing installer metadata explicitly and fail closed.

findings.title: Compare immutable GitHub user IDs instead of logins
findings.body: The authorization decision compares the current OAuth user's login with a login stored from an installation webhook. GitHub usernames can change and old usernames can be acquired by another account. An account that acquires the installer's old username can therefore pass this check for an unlinked installation, while the actual installer will be rejected after renaming their account. Store and compare the immutable GitHub user ID available in both the webhook sender and authenticated user response instead.
